title: Character realizations of Schubert polynomials
statement: For each finite permutation \(w\), find a finite-dimensional polynomial representation, in a specified group category, whose torus character equals \(\mathfrak S_w\).
status: As of November 2026, the Borel-module formulation is solved by Kra\'skiewicz--Pragacz, in a 1986 preprint announced in 1987 and fully published in 2004. These modules need not be irreducible; the seminar does not specify a category for its stronger irreducibility wording. \citep[Theorem 4.1 and Introduction]{kraskiewiczpragacz2004schubert}

title: Real and complex representability of a finite matroid
statement: Given a finite matroid by its bases, determine whether it is representable over \(\mathbb R\) or over \(\mathbb C\).
status: As of November 2026, the finite decision problem is settled by polynomial encoding and quantifier elimination, available before 1987. The broader phrase classification is not made into a separate unresolved claim without a specified structural target. This is distinct from earlier problems on realization-space topology and determinant-sign isotopy. \citep[\S\S 2--3]{tarski1951decision}

title: Axiomatizing the nonzero-minor data of a bimatroid
statement: Characterize abstract collections \(\mathcal R\) of equally sized row-column subset pairs by axioms generalizing nonzero square minors.
status: As of November 2026, the collection is a bimatroid exactly when \(\{(E\setminus I)\sqcup J:(I,J)\in\mathcal R\}\) is a matroid basis family on \(E\sqcup F\) containing \(E\). The checked modern exposition attributes the theory to Kung 1978. \citep[Proposition 2.2]{rohrleulirsch2026bimatroids}

title: Information in a bimatroid beyond its row and column matroids
statement: Determine what data of a matrix bimatroid are lost when only its row matroid and column matroid are retained.
status: As of November 2026, the separate matroids do not determine the bimatroid; a two-by-two counterexample is given in the occurrence. Joint submatrix ranks, equivalently the nonzero square-minor pairs subject to bimatroid axioms, supply the missing data. \citep[Proposition 2.6]{rohrleulirsch2026bimatroids}

title: Generic irreducible Hecke characters in symmetric functions
statement: For the semisimple type-A Hecke algebra \(H_N(q)\), give a symmetric-function formula for irreducible character values on standard cycle elements \(T_{w_\mu}\).
status: As of November 2026, a Frobenius formula is available; Ram published one in 1991, and Halverson--Ram give the exact normalization and credit several independent discoveries. This is a generic-parameter answer and does not settle the different root-of-unity decomposition problem. \citep[equation (4.10), Theorem 4.11]{halversonram1999bitraces}

title: Joint spectra of row-stochastic matrices
statement: For each \(n\), give necessary and sufficient conditions on a complex multiset \((1,\lambda_2,\ldots,\lambda_n)\) to be the spectrum of a real nonnegative \(n\times n\) matrix with every row sum equal to one.
status: As of 11 November 2026: partly characterized. The order-three region was known before the talk; recent geometric and prescribed-pattern results do not give a general explicit solution in orders at least five \citep[p.~506]{ranteng2024patterns}\citep[Sections~4--5, 8]{johnsonpaparella2025perron}. Section~\ref{dev:stochastic} supplies complete two- and three-state realizations and proves that even all JLL inequalities are insufficient in order five. Fixed-order algebraic feasibility is decidable, so the unresolved goal is a useful structural characterization with realizing matrices, rather than bare decidability.

title: Geometric invariants of equivariant toric bundles from filtrations
statement: Compute cohomology, weight characters and Chern classes of an equivariant vector bundle on a smooth complete toric variety directly from its compatible ray filtrations.
status: 2026-11: solved in Klyachko's 1989 paper (English translation 1990), Theorems 3.2.1,4.1.1,4.2.1.

title: Moduli of compatible filtrations and toric bundles
statement: For fixed fan, rank and equivariant Chern data, construct and analyze the moduli of compatible ray filtrations modulo change of basis; distinguish this from a finite indecomposable list for an arbitrary simplicial complex.
status: 2026-11: toric fixed-data moduli spaces are constructed; rank-three examples satisfy Murphy's law (Payne2008). This supplies a moduli formulation, with no assertion of finite-type representation classification for every complex.

title: Cauchy double-alternant determinant
statement: Evaluate \(\det(1/(x_i-y_j))\) under the nonvanishing denominator hypotheses.
status: 2026-11: classical solved identity; the factorization and sign convention are given in the occurrence entry.

title: Real zeros in the Legendre Rodrigues formula
statement: Prove that the nth derivative of \((x^2-1)^n\) has n real simple zeros in \((-1,1)\).
status: 2026-11: classical, by Rolle's theorem or orthogonality.

title: Possible discontinuities of Baire-class-one functions
statement: For a pointwise limit of real continuous functions on an interval, determine whether discontinuities can occur, be dense, or fill the interval.
status: 2026-11: yes to the first two; no to the last, by Baire's theorem.

title: Normalized conformal maps of the slit and dumbbell domains
statement: Construct a disk map for a radially slit disk, and establish a normalized disk map for a simply connected dumbbell domain with its marked interior point sent to0.
status: 2026-11: classical mapping theory settles existence; the slit case has an elementary composition. The picture alone does not specify a numerical dumbbell map.

title: Principal-angle classification and realization in finite dimension
statement: For two subspaces of fixed dimensions k,m in an n-dimensional positive inner-product space, determine a complete orthogonal or unitary orbit invariant and all its attainable values, including realization relative to a fixed first subspace.
status: 2026-11: solved classical problem. The ordered principal angles lie in [0,pi/2], with at least max(0,k+m-n) zeros; these are exactly the restrictions.

title: Angles and attainable invariants of tensor subspaces
statement: For nonzero \(a,b\in L\otimes L\) with finite-dimensional positive inner-product L, classify the pair \(a\otimes L,L\otimes b\subset L^{\otimes3}\) by principal angles and determine their full possible range.
status: 2026-11: the chapter annotation at Section~\ref{dev:tensor-angles} proves that for \(\dim L=d\ge2\), precisely the nonnegative ordered principal cosines of sum at most one occur; for d=1 only cosine one occurs. The result is presented as a worked solution of an established linear-algebra exercise, without a novelty claim.

title: Pairs of subspaces in finite-dimensional indefinite or degenerate forms
statement: Fix a finite-dimensional real vector space with a symmetric bilinear form, possibly indefinite or degenerate. Classify ordered pairs of subspaces under the full group preserving that form, including null subspaces.
status: 2026-11: finite-dimensional canonical forms are available in Sergeichuk (1990). This does not transfer to the unspecified infinite-dimensional indefinite variant.

title: Complete invariants and realization for closed Hilbert-subspace pairs
statement: Classify an ordered pair of closed Hilbert subspaces under ambient isometries, retaining both discrete intersections and the generic spectral invariant; determine the admissible data and give discrete and continuous examples.
status: 2026-11: solved by the two-projection canonical form (Halmos, 1969). The invariant includes spectral measure class and multiplicity, not just the spectrum as a set; dimension constraints govern realization.

title: Configurations of at most three linear subspaces
statement: Classify one subspace, ordered pairs and ordered triples of subspaces of a finite-dimensional real or complex vector space under GL, and characterize the attainable invariant data.
status: 2026-11: solved finite-type classification; triples have eight one-dimensional membership blocks and one two-dimensional three-line block, with nine nonnegative multiplicities.

title: Four-subspace classification and operator encoding
statement: Classify ordered quadruples in a finite-dimensional vector space up to simultaneous linear isomorphism, and include the similarity problem for one operator through its graph configuration.
status: 2026-11: the algebraically closed characteristic-zero problem was classified by Gelfand--Ponomarev in 1971 using explicit indecomposable families. It is an established result explicitly recalled in this problem sheet.

title: An intrinsic regularity criterion for local functionals
statement: Characterize when a scalar functional on an open subset of \(C^\infty(M)\) is, locally in configuration space, an integral of a smooth finite-jet density; determine what must supplement disjoint-support additivity.
status: 2026-11: continuity and additivity alone are insufficient, as point evaluation shows. Under Bastiani smoothness, smooth-density differential and smooth dependence of the gradient, the exact local finite-jet characterization is proved by Brouder et al. (preprint2017; publication2018).

title: Relations among quantum Miura coefficients
statement: For independent Heisenberg currents and \(L=:(D+v_1)\cdots(D+v_N):\), determine the singular operator products of the coefficient fields and prove closure of the resulting quantum Gelfand--Dikii algebra.
status: 2026-11: solved in Lukyanov (1988), received25February1988 before the Radul report. Theorem 1 gives quadratic closure, Section 2 its regularity relation and explicit coefficients, and Theorem 2 the reduced \(W_N\) construction.

title: Variational calculus for products and multilocal functionals
statement: Extend variational differentiation from local scalar functionals to finite sums and products, while distinguishing that generated algebra from arbitrary smooth kernels depending on jets at several base points.
status: 2026-11: finite products satisfy the ordinary iterated Leibniz calculus. Rigorous smooth-functional and multilocal settings are developed, including Brouder et al. (2017/2018). A topology and a specified class of kernels are needed for questions about completion; the notebook states no unique such completion problem.

title: Hearts realizing the derived category of a quiver
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field and Q a finite acyclic quiver. Describe bounded t-structures on \(D^b(\operatorname{rep}_kQ)\) whose heart \(\mathcal A\) is a finite-length abelian k-category with a projective generator and finite-dimensional Hom spaces, and whose realization functor \(D^b(\mathcal A)\to D^b(\operatorname{rep}_kQ)\) is an equivalence.
status: The Dynkin algebra endpoint was established by \citet[Theorem~5.12]{happel1987derived} in 1987, after an Ottawa 1984 announcement. Parthasarathy's December 1988 publication supplies the precise t-structure-data realization criterion and construction reported here; this later refinement is the class-B publication match. Receipt on 15 February 1988 is not itself proof of public circulation before the seminar. Arbitrary embedded abelian subcategories are outside the identified theorem.

title: Fermat's last theorem
statement: For every integer \(n>2\), there are no positive integers \(a,b,c\) with \(a^n+b^n=c^n\). Finiteness of rational points on a fixed genus-greater-than-one curve does not by itself prove this nonexistence statement.
status: Settled by the modularity method published in 1995; the 1988 marginal mention of Faltings did not settle the equation.

title: Four-colour theorem and reducibility
statement: Does every finite loopless planar graph admit a proper four-colouring?
status: Settled by Appel and Haken in 1976, published in 1977; a complete formal proof was subsequently constructed by Gonthier.

title: Riemann hypothesis
statement: Every zero \(\rho\) of the analytically continued Riemann zeta function with \(0<\Re\rho<1\) satisfies \(\Re\rho=1/2\).
status: Open as of 11 November 2026, as confirmed by the official Clay problem page.

title: Parallel implementation of configuration reducibility tests
statement: Given a finite ring configuration, implement a specified sound finite reducibility test based on boundary colourings and compatible Kempe data, allowing independent colourings/configurations to be processed in parallel. No machine model, complexity bound or completeness criterion for all notions of reducibility is stated.
status: Established finite reducibility algorithms and later verified implementations give a partial match; the exact parallel architecture and requested performance were never specified. No new complexity claim is made.

title: Microlocal reconstruction of perverse sheaves
statement: Let \(X\) be a complex manifold and \(\Lambda\subset T^*X\) a specified closed complex analytic conic Lagrangian. With coefficients in \(\mathbb C\), describe the category of perverse sheaves with singular support in \(\Lambda\) by local Morse data on the smooth pieces, gluing at codimension-one loci, and explicit compatibility conditions at singular loci. A complete answer must characterize the essential image, not only embed the category faithfully.
status: Partial over complex coefficients: GMV 2005 proves the fully faithful embedding and the codimension-one equivalence; Kashiwara--Vilonen 2014 (announced 2010, full preprint 2012) proves extension across codimension at least three. Their Problem~9.3, p.~617, explicitly asks for the geometric codimension-two conditions on the essential image. No general solution to that remaining task was identified through 11 November 2026.
